sandbox.description: Send requests to Amazon's SP-API sandbox, which returns fixed example responses. For testing only.
sandbox.title: Use Sandbox

window_size.description: Size of the date windows orders and financial transactions are requested in, in ISO 8601 format. E.g. P1D means 1 day, PT6H means 6 hours. The daily orders sweep uses these windows too. Orders backfill doubles windows with at most half a page of orders up to 30 days and retains smaller windows after rejected pagination tokens. Each order window must be paged through within 24 hours, so busy accounts may need smaller windows.
window_size.title: Window Size

overlap.description: How far each incremental request reaches back before the previous one ended, to catch orders Amazon makes searchable late, in ISO 8601 format. The daily sweep also re-reads each update after it is Orders Lookback old for longer indexing delays.
overlap.title: Incremental Overlap

orders_lookback.description: How old each order update must be before the daily orders sweep re-reads it once, in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to PT48H; minimum PT1H. Runs at backfill priority, independently of the incremental cursor, when at least a day of updates is due. Orders Amazon makes searchable later than Orders Lookback after their update are missed. Completed windows are checkpointed so interrupted sweeps resume from the last window.
orders_lookback.title: Orders Lookback

financial_transactions_lookback.description: How far behind the present financial transactions are read a final time, to catch deferred transactions Amazon has since released, in ISO 8601 format. Deferred transactions, such as invoiced (B2B) orders, are released on their maturity date, so set this past the longest deferral the account sees. Changes to a transaction after this point are not captured. Raising it re-reads the newly covered time.
financial_transactions_lookback.title: Financial Transactions Lookback

refresh_token.description: The refresh token issued when the selling account authorized the application.
refresh_token.title: Refresh Token

region.description: The SP-API region of the selling account. Capture each region separately.

marketplace_ids.description: Amazon marketplace IDs to capture, such as ATVPDKIKX0DER for Amazon.com. All must belong to the selected region.
marketplace_ids.title: Marketplace IDs

start_date.description: UTC date and time in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Orders created, financial transactions posted, settlement reports created and all orders lines last updated before this date are not captured, nor Sales and Traffic days before the UTC day it falls in. Amazon serves about two years of order history, and of all orders and Sales and Traffic reports, but keeps settlement reports for only 90 days, so older data is not captured whatever this date. If left blank, the start date is set to 30 days before the date each stream first starts backfilling.
start_date.title: Start Date

interval.description: Interval between updates for this resource
interval.title: Interval

schedule.description: Schedule to automatically rebackfill this binding. Accepts a cron expression.
schedule.title: Schedule
